cases.summary: "Lost an owner context" error while trying to complete a Join activity using WaitAny, on a workflow using a before/after/always commit strategy.
cases.description: ## Description This happens because of how Elsa Workflows handles flowchart completion together with the commit behavior. When a workflow contains a Join Activity with WaitAny, that joins together several branches, out of which at least one contain a loop (with it's own flowchart): The flowchart is marked as completed before the Join activity is scheduled. When the Commit option is set to “Always Commit” or "Commit Before/After Activity Execution", the workflow state is saved to the database at every step, including exactly when the Join executes. At that moment, the commit logic runs and attempts to process the Join’s completion callback. However, since the flowchart has already been marked as completed (and completed flowcharts are filtered out), it can no longer find the flowchart context. ## Steps to Reproduce I've attached the workflow definition used for reproducing this: and this is the result: 1. **Detailed Steps**: You can also try this by creating a workflow that has two branches, one with a simple 5 seconds delay, the other one with a simple 1-iteration for loop that also contains a 10 seconds delay. both branches then meet into a Join activity with a "WaitAny" strategy. Make sure you set the workflow strategy to Before/After activity execution or Always Commit. When running the issue "Lost an owner context" will immediately become apparent. 3. **Attachments**: [parallel.delay-lost.owner.context.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25683367/parallel.delay-lost.owner.context.json) 4. **Reproduction Rate**: Every time. ## Expected Behavior Flow should not Fault, Join activity should be completed without incidents. Join activity should not try canceling activities within upstream flowchart before scheduling them. ## Actual Behavior Flow goes into faulted state with incidents. Join activity does not complete; output states "Lost an owner context exception". ## Environment - **Elsa Package Version**: 3.5.* - **Operating System**: Windows 11 / any. - **Browser and Version**: fix: 7335 - Call ScheduleOutboundActivityAsync before calling CancelRemainingInboundActivitiesAsync …

… in order to avoid the "Lost an owner context" exception.

Issue description: this was happenning because of how Elsa Workflows handles flowchart completion together with the commit behavior. When a workflow contains a Join Activity with WaitAny, that joins together several branches, out of which at least one contain a loop (with it's own flowchart): The flowchart is marked as completed before the Join activity is scheduled. When the Commit option is set to “Always Commit”, the workflow state is saved to the database at every step, including exactly when the Join executes. At that moment, the commit logic runs and attempts to process the Join’s completion callback. However, since the flowchart has already been marked as completed (and completed flowcharts are filtered out), it can no longer find the flowchart context.

## Purpose
Call ScheduleOutboundActivityAsync before calling CancelRemainingInboundActivitiesAsync in order to avoid the "Lost an owner context" exception.

## Description

### Problem
This resolves a "Lost an owner context" exception described in https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-core/issues/7335.

### Solution
By scheduling the activities ahead of calling the cancelation, this avoids situations in which scheduling is attempted on activities that are part of a FlowChart that has already been canceled.

---

## Verification
Run the workflow definition attached to the mentioned issue.

Steps:
1. Import the worklfow definition
2. Run an instance of the provided definition

Expected outcome:
The workflow should end up in state Finished without incidents.
